A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same pCQO-MIS research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original solver evaluations on SATLIB, ER and GNM graphs, including benchmark performance, scalability, sensitivity and MIS-checking experiments.

after.justification: v4 reports original benchmark results and adds DIMACS evaluations, joint parameter ablations and results across optimization batch budgets.

M1.justification: Section 3.3.4 replaces v2's two restart alternatives with previous-best-vector sampling and explicitly carries momentum between batches. Previous-best sampling already existed as pCQO-MIS-2; momentum carryover revises the described procedure, although Algorithm 1 still initializes velocity to zero. The objective, gradient updates and MIS-checking criterion remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds evaluation on 61 DIMACS instances, including structured graph families associated with coding theory, fault diagnosis and Keller's conjecture. This substantially broadens coverage beyond the retained SATLIB and random ER/GNM evaluations.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain the same external comparators: ReduMIS, CP-SAT, Gurobi, GCN, LwD, DIMES, both DIFUSCO decoding variants, iSCO and dNN-MIS. The new DIMACS experiment reuses ReduMIS. Updated scores and removal of separately reported proposed-method variants do not introduce a new external baseline.

E3.justification: Table 1 switches iSCO timing from extrapolated sequential execution to parallel graph evaluation, with sequential estimates supplied separately. Section 4.2 narrows the stated 30-second cap to ER exact-solver results. Added protocols include the 30-second DIMACS comparison and six-graph joint parameter sweeps replacing v2's ten-graph gamma-only sweep. These are reported protocol differences, not proof that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: v2's gamma-only sensitivity study is replaced by step-size/momentum and gamma/gamma-prime ablations in Tables 7–8. Tables 9–10 add detailed performance-versus-batch analyses, while the separate comparison of restart variants disappears. The MC-term ablation, density-transfer comparison, MIS-checking experiment and stationary-point study remain, with some relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed evaluation, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates. Both report averages across graph instances. The newly documented optimization batch counts are computational budgets, not statistical repetitions.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces eight variant rows with four revised pCQO-MIS rows. For example, v2's best ER entry is 45 at 62.93 minutes, whereas v4 reports 45.109 at 54.766 minutes; changed restart/budget descriptions limit direct performance comparison. iSCO scores and Figure 3 runtimes also change. DIMACS, parameter and batch results are added. DIMACS Table 3 contains 48 optimum matches for pCQO-MIS versus 58 for ReduMIS, although Appendix D.1 claims 49.

T1.justification: Appendix A changes several theorem restatements and proof references from maximum independent sets to maximal independent sets, including broadening Theorem 1's restatement and narrowing Theorem 2's guarantee. The main-text statements are not consistently updated, and most derivations remain unchanged. Remark 1 also changes the stated computational cost from O(m+n) to O(mn) without a new derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: a dataless clique-informed quadratic objective, theoretical characterizations, parallel momentum optimization, efficient MIS checking and competitive performance. The conclusion's optimizer wording is aligned with the already-described method; the expanded evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix D.5 broadens the low-sensitivity interpretation from gamma alone to several optimization parameters, while excluding poor small-step settings. v2's interpretation that previous-best restarts particularly benefit SATLIB is removed. Existing explanations concerning sparse-graph solvers, generalization and saddle-point infeasibility largely remain.

D1.justification: v4 newly states that the implementation uses C++, supplies an own-code access link, documents GNM and DIMACS hyperparameters, identifies iSCO hardware and links benchmark results to explicit batch budgets. The SATLIB/ER hyperparameter values are retained. Newly disclosed implementation and GNM settings do not establish that those underlying choices changed.

R1.justification: v4 replaces the genome-assembly citation, removes the placeholder multi-robot reference and adds references for Gamarnik's GNN discussion, Polyak's momentum method, CP-SAT, DIMACS and a maximum-clique survey. It also locally revises the GCN-randomization and dataless-GNN discussions. The overall related-work categories and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: The main narrative and most method prose are retained. Edits refine experimental and related-work passages, repair unresolved citations and replace the conclusion's inconsistent Adam reference with momentum-based gradient descent. The appendices are reorganized: the stationary-point study becomes Appendix B, related work becomes C, and the MIS-checking experiment moves from Section 4.4 to D.2.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redesigned from a plot-plus-table display into a wide runtime plot with a zoomed inset and graph-size/MIS-size axis labels. Table 1 consolidates the proposed-method rows. New DIMACS, ablation and batch tables substantially expand the displays. Existing checking and stationary-point figures are relocated, and the old gamma-sensitivity chart is removed.

improvement.justification: The DIMACS evaluation makes comparative weaknesses against ReduMIS more assessable, while broader ablations, documented code access, GNM settings and batch budgets improve empirical transparency over v2. These benefits are partly offset by inconsistencies introduced in v4: the DIMACS prose/table optimum count differs, some SATLIB runtimes disagree between Tables 1 and 9, and momentum-carryover prose conflicts with Algorithm 1. The evidence supports a limited overall quality gain.
